name: Dictation Typer
tagline: Hold, speak, release — it types into whatever has focus.
summary: A hold-to-talk speech-to-text utility. Audio is held in memory, transcribed on hosted Whisper with an optional offline fallback, and pasted straight into the focused window.

authorship.role: Sole author — hotkey capture, transcription routing and privacy mode.
built: The hold-hotkey capture loop with in-memory WAV streaming and no disk writes
Privacy mode, which requires confirmation before audio leaves the machine when no offline model is configured
Paste-into-focused-window handling, Windows-native with documented fallbacks
notBuilt: Whisper itself — hosted transcription and the optional local faster-whisper model are both existing implementations

caseStudy.problem: Dictation is built into most operating systems and is consistently worse than hosted Whisper. The gap is not the model, it is the plumbing: getting audio to a good model and the text back into whatever application currently has focus, fast enough that it beats typing.
caseStudy.approach: Bind everything to one held hotkey, keep the audio in memory as a streamed WAV so nothing touches disk, and paste into the active window rather than requiring a dedicated interface. Make cloud transcription refusable: in privacy mode, audio is not sent unless the user confirms or an offline model is configured.

visuals.alt: Illustration of a hotkey-driven dictation flow ending in text pasted into an editor
visuals.caption: Illustration of the capture flow. Not a screenshot — no capture of the running tool has been published yet.

outcomes.statement: Nothing touches disk except opt-in crash logs — audio is streamed as an in-memory WAV.

tradeoffs.choice: Hosted transcription by default with an optional local model
tradeoffs.gained: Fast, accurate and near-free transcription without shipping a multi-gigabyte model.
tradeoffs.gaveUp: The default path sends audio off the machine, which is why privacy mode and the offline fallback both exist.

tradeoffs.choice: Windows-native, with documented notes for macOS and Linux
tradeoffs.gained: The focused-window paste behaviour actually works properly on the primary platform.
tradeoffs.gaveUp: Cross-platform support is best-effort rather than first-class.

limitations: A personal utility, never hardened for distribution; its source was removed during the 2026-08 ecosystem migration.

sourceRemoved.note: Source no longer exists in the monorepo (removed from apps/registry.json on main). Kept as a historical case study.
